summary: Handle the one-Number Array constructor form as a length, producing holes rather than elements.

target.notes: Validate the numeric length exactly as the Array constructor does and create a sparse array with no own indexed elements.

semantics.valid_length: integral Number in [0, 2^32-1]; -0 is accepted as 0

caveats: new Array(3) is not [3]; indices 0..2 are absent properties.
NaN, infinities, fractional values, negative values, and 2^32 or larger throw RangeError.
Filling a C# list with null/default values is observably wrong because holes are not present undefined elements.

tests.name: numeric argument creates holes
tests.input: const a = Array(3); console.log(a.length, 0 in a, a[0]);
